liveEndpointCheck.method: Independent TLS-layer checks against eurolive.jp:443 using two separate client stacks (curl/schannel and OpenSSL 3.5.5 s_client), across TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3, repeated 3 times.
liveEndpointCheck.result: Every attempt completes the TCP connection but the server aborts the TLS handshake with a server-originated 'tlsv1 alert internal error' (TLS alert 80) before any certificate or application data is exchanged. The same failure occurs on the related parent domain www.eurospace.co.jp, which shares the same hosting. This is a server-side fault, not a client compatibility gap: OpenSSL 3.5.5 and Windows schannel independently agree the server itself terminates the handshake.
liveEndpointCheck.conclusion: No current official HTTPS endpoint exists for the eurolive.jp domain family. The operator's only currently working web transport is plain HTTP; WebFetch's automatic http-to-https upgrade fails for exactly this reason, which is why the seat-chart evidence in the prior preflight and this implementation attempt was fetched via curl over HTTP.

transportPolicyCheck.conclusion: The HTTPS requirement is a hard, unconditional, source-status-independent gate in the current schema/validator, not a soft production-only check, and no current official HTTPS issuer endpoint exists for this venue. Per the prohibitions on rewriting a URL to https:// without verification, weakening validation, substituting an unofficial mirror as the official source, and lowering the currentness/evidence gate, no venue source JSON may be authored for tokyo-official-0635 under the existing repository contract. This is a repository transport-policy blocker, not an evidence gap: the seat chart itself is current, complete, and issuer-numbered (see twoPass below). Disposition: SOURCE/POLICY HOLD. No source, range, production, generated artifact, or fingerprint change was made.
